sections.overview: Diachrysia zosimi is a localized noctuid moth of European wetlands, with scattered populations in parts of its range.
sections.identification: It is a medium-sized member of the gold moth group; the greenish metallic marking on its forewings helps separate it from close Diachrysia species.
sections.habitat: It is stenotopic and chiefly inhabits calcareous fens, transitional mires and riverine wetlands with lush vegetation.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed mainly on great burnet, Sanguisorba officinalis; Finnish records also mention other rose-family plants, but these appear less typical.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in midsummer and are attracted to artificial light; Finnish records also report visits to flowers.
sections.reproduction: The Polish account reports one generation annually. Caterpillars feed from summer into the following spring and overwinter before pupating.
sections.ecology: Because it depends on specialized wetland vegetation and host plants, populations can occupy very small sites and remain isolated from one another.
sections.conservation: It has disappeared from many European localities, and the Polish species account recommends protecting occupied sites; this is not a global status category.
